memos.scout:
The strongest honest case for buying FROGE is the organic-looking distribution and sustained flow. The curve shows 465 buyers, a low top-3 share (7.2%), and a completer share of 26%, which means no single wallet is holding the supply. The first two minutes after graduation saw 340 non-agent buyers spending 184 SOL, with a top-5 buyer share of 22%, and the class is labeled ORGANIC with no airdrop dump. The 15-minute window shows 1,259 buyers and 888 SOL of buy volume against 867 SOL of sells, a net inflow of 21 SOL, and a +2.4% return. The coin is also up roughly 4x over 30 minutes and remains alive.

The case weakens on closer reading. Sell-to-buy in the launch window was 0.97, meaning early buyers were nearly fully exiting. The 15-minute net flow is thin relative to gross volume, and the coin is 32% below its 30-minute high, so momentum has already faded. Bundle share of 33% is high. With a 172 SOL pool, a $20 round trip faces meaningful impact. I can make the case for demand persisting, but the evidence supports a small, tentative position at most, not a conviction buy.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss path: distribution into the current bounce. FROGE is up 4.06x over 30 minutes but has already fallen 31.6% from its high, and the last 15 minutes show sell SOL (867.4) almost matching buy SOL (888.46), with 1,073 sellers against 1,259 buyers and net flow only +21 SOL. That looks like early holders exiting into retail demand, not a fresh wave of conviction.

The launch was bot-assisted, and the first two minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.97, so the exit pattern is already established. Pool depth of 172 SOL is thin relative to $190k market cap, so a $20 buy plus a $20 exit could cost 1.4-5.1% before any move. A 3-5% bounce could be erased by a single seller wave, and dead volume after the next leg down would leave a round trip underwater. Skip.
